title: Empowering Teachers with Enhanced Knowledge via Variable Scale Distillation Framework

contributions.purpose: Better exploit the teacher network's superior feature-extraction capacity in knowledge distillation, which prior methods under-utilize by feeding teacher and student identical inputs.
contributions.mechanism: Variable Scale Distillation Framework: train the teacher on images of varying (higher) resolutions (inspired by image super-resolution) so it captures both high-level semantics and fine details, combined with multi-task training that mixes self-supervised (rotation pretext) learning with image classification in an aggregated vector space.
contributions.evaluation: CIFAR100 with ResNet/WideResNet/VGG/ShuffleNet/MobileNet backbones; consistently outperforms SOTA distillation, average accuracy improvement of 2.12%; up to 5.59% gain over best competitor on ResNet32x4->ResNet8x4.
contributions.source_quote: Variable Scale Distillation Framework: In this novel framework, we enable the teacher network to learn more fine-grained semantic features from high-resolution images, allowing the student model to absorb richer knowledge.

contributions.purpose: Fix the feature-map size mismatch between teacher (fed larger/finer images) and student (original size) that breaks hierarchical distillation.
contributions.mechanism: A Rescale Block that preserves scale consistency between teacher and student feature maps during hierarchical distillation, aligning feature maps so the student can mimic the teacher's hierarchical dark knowledge.
contributions.evaluation: Ablation (Table 1) on SSKD shows the Variable Scale Framework + Rescale Block yields significant student accuracy improvements across configurations.
contributions.source_quote: Rescale Block: By maintaining scale consistency between teacher and student feature maps, we solve the feature mismatch problem, ensuring the effectiveness of knowledge transfer.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate generalization of the framework across tasks and datasets.
contributions.mechanism: Comprehensive comparison against SOTA KD methods (KD, CRD, SSKD, HSAKD, etc.) across 10 teacher-student pairs (same and different architectures), few-shot scenarios (25/50/75% data), and transfer via frozen-encoder linear classification.
contributions.evaluation: Best on all 5 same-architecture pairs; in 25% few-shot achieves 70.50% (vs KD's 70.66% with 100% data); frozen student encoder outperforms all baselines on STL10 and TinyImageNet linear classification.
contributions.source_quote: State-of-the-art Performance: Our method consistently surpasses existing state-of-the-art approaches in tasks such as image classification, few-shot learning, and linear classification, showcasing its generalizability to other downstream applications.

self_declared_provenance.quote: our work presents a novel approach inspired by image super-resolution Ledig et al. (2017). It leverages the teacher network's superior feature extraction capability by presenting it with more detailed, fine-grained image input.
Different from most previous methods, our method incorporates multi-task training, combining self-supervised learning with image classification.

notes: All reported comparisons favor the proposed method; no negative or tie results disclosed (positive-only reporting). Main gains: average +2.12% over SOTA, up to +5.59% on ResNet32x4/ResNet8x4, and strong few-shot result (70.50% at 25% data vs KD 70.66% at 100%). Only CIFAR100 used for the main distillation experiments (STL10/TinyImageNet only for transfer linear-probe). Grafts image-super-resolution intuition and self-supervised multi-task training onto the SSKD/HSAKD line of feature-based distillation.
